title: StatePreparationWiki
scope: A research and formalization agenda, not a claim that all listed questions are open in every model or that ASPBE has improved a lower bound.
resource_contract: oracle construction, inverse and controlled access
primitive gates, T/Toffoli count and depth

baseline.statement: An arbitrary N=2^n dimensional vector is not a succinct structured input. Parameter-counting and access-model lower bounds must be compared in their own precision, gate and ancilla models.
baseline.prohibition: Do not promise universal poly(n) loading of an arbitrary explicitly supplied vector. Do not confuse exponential gate count with ancilla count.

routes.title: High-dimensional structured function states
routes.goal: Prove a constructive cost and state-error theorem for a precisely specified low-rank, sparse-frequency, mixed-smoothness or compositional class; do not equate these assumptions.
routes.motivation: Multivariate PDE data, localized scientific functions and conditional distributions need more than generic amplitude loading.
routes.input_model: An explicit formula-to-core supplier or a charged sparse coefficient oracle; grid, complex phase and a nonzero norm are part of the input.
assumptions: D and n specified; rank r and degree q are certified, not numerical fit labels
Core/coefficients and normalizer are computably supplied
Approximation error includes model compression, grid, arithmetic and primitive synthesis
routes.target_bound: A candidate target is poly(D,r,q,n,log(1/epsilon)) cost under stated bit-length and stability promises; this bound is not claimed here.
routes.known_boundary: Generic tensor-product degree-q expansions have (q+1)^D coefficients; smoothness alone does not remove dimensionality. Hermite's one-dimensional exact-real compiler is a substrate, not this multivariate theorem.

steps.target: Choose one function class and prove a uniform rank/degree certificate.
steps.acceptance: A source-faithful class predicate and formula-to-core action theorem, including phases and supports.

steps.target: Bound normalized-state error from core approximation and arithmetic.
steps.acceptance: An explicit norm lower bound and a theorem for the exact requested vector norm; no uncharged condition number.

steps.target: Compose the class supplier with the existing clean TT compiler.
steps.acceptance: Primitive-list semantics, workspace cleanup, and every cost coordinate under the same model.

routes.next: Start from the Hermite corridor; add a tensor-product or shallow coupled class with a proved rank bound before claiming general high dimension.

lower_bound.task: Separate arbitrary-vector counting barriers from lower bounds for the selected structured class. Specify which class parameters enter the hard family.

benchmarks: Product Gaussian with explicitly bounded widths
Weakly coupled Gaussian with a proved rank estimate

routes.title: Preconditioned function preparation with an explicit envelope
routes.goal: Construct g for one useful localized function class so that reference preparation, ratio implementation and amplification are all controlled.
routes.motivation: Uniform-state postselection can have exponentially small filling fraction in dimension; a reference should match localization without hiding an equally hard preparation problem.
routes.input_model: A clean U_g and U_g-dagger with charged construction; coherent access to a bounded complex ratio; classical or certified scalar C.
assumptions: support(f) subset support(g); define the ratio as zero off support(g)
f and g nonzero and C>0
A constructive domination certificate, not an empirical maximum on a few grid points
routes.target_bound: For a selected class, prove kappa_env and reference/ratio costs polynomial in declared class parameters; add a model-matched obstruction or lower bound.
routes.known_boundary: Coherent rejection and reweighting are prior art. Uniform g recovers kappa_env=1/F2 where F2=||f||2/(sqrt(M)||f||infinity). A small ratio on average does not imply a valid pointwise envelope.

steps.target: Formalize support-aware coherent reweighting and its exact success probability.
steps.acceptance: All amplitudes including zero-reference entries and complex phases agree; normalizer nonzero.

steps.target: Build a certified reference for a restricted localized class.
steps.acceptance: A concrete supplier for g, a global domination proof and kappa bound.

steps.target: Add robust ratio approximation and amplification.
steps.acceptance: State error and actual query/primitive costs, including U_g inversion and repeated calls.

routes.next: First close the support-aware probability identity, then study anisotropic product envelopes and a controlled perturbation class.

lower_bound.task: Audit the quantum rejection-sampling query lower bound and prove whether its oracle assumptions match this structured envelope model before transferring it.

benchmarks: Piecewise payoff functions with declared phase convention

routes.title: Data loading without a free QRAM assumption
routes.formula: T_{\rm total}=T_{\rm build}+Q\,T_{\rm query}+T_{\rm update}+T_{\rm readout}
routes.goal: Identify succinct data classes for which explicit access construction preserves the intended algorithmic advantage.
routes.motivation: An algorithm with few abstract queries can still be expensive when the query unitary is built from real data.
routes.input_model: Classical stored arrays, QROM, arithmetic formulas and physical QRAM are separate settings with explicit initialization, updates and memory costs.
assumptions: Fix data bit length, update frequency and reuse count
Charge controlled/inverse queries when the algorithm uses them
Compare against a classical algorithm with the same access assumptions
routes.target_bound: A full cost theorem for one succinct data representation, not universal polylogarithmic loading of an arbitrary array.
routes.known_boundary: General sparse-access and block-encoding constructions can require near-linear cost in matrix dimension. Sparsity does not make all entries free.

steps.target: Define the exact classical/quantum access interface.
steps.acceptance: Separate data construction, coherent calls, memory and update costs.

steps.target: Compile one formula, sparse-index or repeated-block supplier.
steps.acceptance: Basis-action theorem and count of actual access primitives.

steps.target: Reinsert access costs into a downstream algorithm.
steps.acceptance: A comparison using the same input/output model and total cost, not query count alone.

routes.next: Reuse existing sparse/LCU routes only after auditing their oracle contracts and compiler frontiers.

lower_bound.task: Port a pinned circuit-capacity/access lower bound with precision and ancilla assumptions intact.

benchmarks: Sparse matrices with formulaic index/value access

routes.title: Coherent parameter-dependent families
routes.goal: Produce one coherent template for jointly structured parameters and data with a uniform error bound.
routes.motivation: Parameterized PDEs, source histories and Bayesian conditional states require superpositions of inputs, not separate classically compiled circuits.
routes.input_model: Parameter a is a quantum register; one shared joint coefficient/core supplier is provided with a uniform norm bound.
assumptions: Relative phases are fixed across a
Norms stay bounded away from zero on the promised parameter domain
Branch selection and numerical rank changes are controlled coherently or avoided
routes.target_bound: Polynomial dependence on the joint structural parameters and parameter bit length, rather than a table of independent preparations.
routes.known_boundary: A family of individually easy states need not have an easy coherent supplier. Per-parameter correctness up to phase is insufficient.

steps.target: Define the coherent family contract including phases and clean workspace.
steps.acceptance: One matrix action for arbitrary parameter superpositions.

steps.target: Derive a joint tensor/polynomial representation.
steps.acceptance: Uniform rank/degree and nonzero normalization proof over all allowed parameters.

steps.target: Compile with uniform error and cost.
steps.acceptance: Operator-action error on the whole parameter-data subspace, not only sampled parameter values.

routes.next: Use an affine parameterized Hermite or Gaussian family as a small exact model before time-dependent PDE source histories.

lower_bound.task: Keep arbitrary CQSP lower bounds separate from the restricted joint-structure promise.

routes.title: Useful trial states for strong-correlation ground-state preparation
routes.goal: For a specified physical family, construct a cheap trial-state supplier with a proved useful overlap or target-subspace guarantee.
routes.motivation: Near-optimal filtering is only useful when trial-state and spectral promises are available.
routes.input_model: Hamiltonian access, a charged trial-state circuit and explicit energy/gap information; target may be a ground subspace rather than a unique vector.
assumptions: Hamiltonian family and locality stated
Overlap convention and gap promise stated
Trial-state optimization and evaluation costs included
routes.target_bound: A class-specific overlap and total preparation theorem; no unconditional removal of inverse-overlap or inverse-gap barriers.
routes.known_boundary: Lin–Tong provides algorithms and lower bounds under overlap/gap assumptions. Strong correlation does not itself certify an MPS rank or overlap.

steps.target: Formalize one pinned filtering theorem with exact promises.
steps.acceptance: Gap, overlap, energy information and success convention match the source.

steps.target: Prove an overlap bound for a concrete trial family.
steps.acceptance: The trial circuit and overlap certificate are both explicit.

steps.target: Compose trial preparation and filtering.
steps.acceptance: All repeated preparations, oracle calls, error and workspace are charged.

routes.next: Begin with a controlled family with a rigorous trial-state overlap, not arbitrary strongly correlated molecules.

lower_bound.task: Retain search/approximate-counting barriers from the pinned source and test whether extra structure changes their applicability.

benchmarks: Gapped one-dimensional families with a supplied rank certificate
Small selected-CI/MPS trial models with explicit overlap

routes.title: Low-temperature Gibbs preparation with quantitative mixing
routes.goal: For a restricted noncommuting local Hamiltonian family, prove a mixing certificate and implemented-channel error bound.
routes.motivation: An invariant Gibbs state does not guarantee that an implementable sampler reaches it quickly at low temperature.
routes.input_model: Specified Hamiltonian and KMS generator with charged simulation access, temperature, initial state and convergence norm.
assumptions: Primitivity/ergodicity or invariant-subspace restriction stated
Spectral or functional-inequality mixing certificate supplied
Generator implementation and statistical output contract specified
routes.target_bound: A model-specific polynomial mixing and total-cost theorem in the promised temperature regime.
routes.known_boundary: KMS detailed balance and stationarity are not polynomial mixing. Classical sampling inequalities cannot be transferred to quantum operators without a hypothesis map.

steps.target: Port a finite-dimensional invariant-state identity.
steps.acceptance: Exact generator, Gibbs normalizer and adjoint convention.

steps.target: Identify and prove a coercivity or mixing condition for one class.
steps.acceptance: An explicit rate with temperature/system-size dependence; no assumed conclusion.

steps.target: Compose mixing with generator-simulation error.
steps.acceptance: A trace-norm output theorem and total implementation budget.

routes.next: Use a finite-dimensional warm-up and then separate the high-temperature baseline from the intended low-temperature regime.

lower_bound.task: State the oracle and Hamiltonian class before importing hardness or mixing obstructions.

routes.title: Fault-tolerant resource trade-offs for structured preparation
routes.goal: Compile the exact-real structured route into a finite gate set with a proved error budget and declared connectivity.
routes.motivation: A small number of arbitrary real rotations is not a complete fault-tolerant resource estimate.
routes.input_model: Finite-bit source data and a fixed Clifford+T gate set, connectivity graph, tolerance and ancilla policy.
assumptions: Input/separation and conditioning promises exposed
Each angle approximation and synthesis error budget explicit
Count or bound the actual emitted primitive list
routes.target_bound: A source-to-finite-bit theorem and a model-matched resource frontier; do not claim simultaneous global optimality of every coordinate.
routes.known_boundary: The Hermite exact-real primitive theorem is already a useful substrate. Full bit complexity and stable angle generation are additional obligations.

steps.target: Freeze the finite-bit input and numerical-stability contract.
steps.acceptance: All arbitrary-real comparisons and small pivots have explicit handling.

steps.target: Bound coefficient, canonicalization and angle errors.
steps.acceptance: A normalized-state error theorem tied to supplied bit precision.

steps.target: Compose finite-gate synthesis and connectivity routing.
steps.acceptance: T/Toffoli/depth/ancilla accounting plus final state error and cleanup.

routes.next: Treat the current Hermite bit-complexity boundary as the first local target rather than reopening its exact-real correctness proof.

lower_bound.task: Compare ancilla/depth trade-offs only in the same finite gate and connectivity model.

benchmarks: Hermite baseline versus structured route at matched error

routes.title: Joint design of preparation and experimental verification
routes.goal: Automatically derive a low-sample fidelity witness for a precisely defined structured state class.
routes.motivation: Full tomography is not the correct default output task; preparation structure may enable a cheaper witness.
routes.input_model: Copies or channels producing rho, a specified measurement family, classical target representation and declared IID/noise assumptions.
assumptions: Target and implemented noisy state distinguished
Witness computation and measurement basis-change cost included
Confidence, bias and non-IID handling not silently omitted
routes.target_bound: A witness correctness theorem, finite-sample bound and implementation cost for one state family.
routes.known_boundary: A Lean ideal-circuit proof does not certify noisy hardware. The user-supplied 2609.08414 reference remains primary-source-unavailable in this ledger.

steps.target: Specify the measurement and statistical experiment.
steps.acceptance: Outcome law, confidence and noise assumptions are formal objects.

steps.target: Derive a structure-specific fidelity witness.
steps.acceptance: Unbiasedness or certified one-sided bias and computable observable.

steps.target: Prove sample and basis-change complexity.
steps.acceptance: End-to-end confidence statement with no uncharged target tomography.

routes.next: Verify the primary hardware reference first; start formal work from a small exactly analyzable MPS witness.

lower_bound.task: Distinguish lower bounds for full tomography, fidelity estimation and a promised structured witness.

benchmarks: Small exact MPS with prescribed measurement access

routes.title: CV–DV function preparation and non-Gaussian resources
routes.goal: Relate a declared finite-energy oscillator encoding to qubit-grid preparation with a rigorous embedding and separate resource budgets.
routes.motivation: Schrödingerisation uses auxiliary profiles in both continuous-variable and qubit implementations, but their resources are not interchangeable.
routes.input_model: An explicit isometric embedding V_N, cutoff, grid or Fock truncation, energy/squeezing and non-Gaussian gate model.
assumptions: Finite-energy/domain conditions and target normalization
The embedding and quadrature weights are fixed
CV noise, squeezing and non-Gaussian resources are not counted as free qubits
routes.target_bound: A model-specific conversion, approximation and preparation theorem, not a universal equivalence of CV and DV costs.
routes.known_boundary: The finite Hermite state is a useful first example. No CV–DV equivalence or GKP preparation theorem is currently supplied by this route.

steps.target: Define and prove an isometric finite-to-continuous embedding.
steps.acceptance: Inner products and normalization match the stated quadrature/Fock convention.

steps.target: Prove energy-tail and discretization error for a fixed profile family.
steps.acceptance: All cutoff, domain and regularity hypotheses explicit.

steps.target: Compose preparation and conversion costs.
steps.acceptance: Separate DV gates and CV physical resources plus total state error.

routes.next: Choose a finite-energy Hermite-smoothed profile and one embedding before comparing grid, oscillator or GKP implementations.

lower_bound.task: First specify the energy and non-Gaussian resource model; no cross-model lower-bound transfer is asserted.
